BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r1.claim: Duha is the time when the sun rises high, the beginning of the day; it is used metonymically for its time or with an omitted noun to match the reference to night.
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r1.anchor: هو وقت ارتفاع الشمس وصدر النهار

BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r2.claim: The oath alludes to the morning when God spoke to Moses and the magicians fell prostrate, and when people were gathered at morning; this gives the time special honor.
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r2.anchor: التي كلم الله فيها موسى عليه السلام وألقى فيها السحرة سجدا

BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r3.claim: The duha prayer is unanimously a sunnah; its time begins once the sun is high and ends shortly before noon.
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r3.anchor: وصلاة الضحى سنة بالاتفاق ووقتها إذا علت الشمس إلى قبيل وقت الزوال

BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r4.claim: Abu Hanifa sets the duha prayer at two or four units, with one salutation.
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r4.anchor: وهي عند أبي حنيفة ركعتان أو أربع بتسليمة

BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r5.speaker: مالك
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r5.claim: Malik does not set a fixed upper limit for the number of duha prayer units.

BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r6.speaker: الشافعي
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r6.claim: Al-Shafi‘i and Ahmad set the minimum at two units; al-Shafi‘i says the maximum is twelve, while Ahmad says eight, which most Shafi‘i authorities adopt and al-Nawawi validates in al-Tahqiq.
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r6.anchor: وعند الشافعي وأحمد أقلها ركعتان واختلف في أكثرها فقال الشافعي ثنتا عشرة وقال أحمد ثمان

BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r7.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r7.claim: A sound report says the Prophet prayed eight units of duha in Umm Hani's house on the conquest of Mecca and had also prayed duha before then.
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r7.anchor: وقد صح إن النبي عليه اسلام صلى صلاة الضحى يوم فتح مكة ثماني ركعات وهو في بيت أم هانىء

BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r10.speaker: جعفر الصادق
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r10.claim: Ja‘far al-Sadiq identifies the duha with the morning when God spoke to Moses and the night with the Night Journey.
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r10.anchor: وعن جعفر الصادق رضيعنه أن المراد بالضحى هو الضحى الذي كلم الله فيه موسى وبالليل ليلة المعراج

BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r11.speaker: صاحب كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r11.claim: Kashf al-Asrar reads day and night as disclosure and veiling, signs of the breeze of divine gentleness and the scorching wind of divine severity, and of beauty's lights and majesty's traces.
BURSEVI:v10p349#3/r11.anchor: مراد از روز وشب كشف وحجا بست كه نشانه نسيم لطف وسموم قهر بود

BURSEVI:v10p350/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p350/r1.speaker: الجنيد
BURSEVI:v10p350/r1.claim: Al-Junayd calls duha the station of witnessing and the settled night the station of ghayn, the clouding over the heart mentioned in a Prophetic report.
BURSEVI:v10p350/r1.anchor: كما قال الجنيد قدس سره والضحى مقام الشهود والليل إذا سجا مقام الغبن الذي قال عليه السلام فيه إنه ليغان على قلبي

BURSEVI:v10p350/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p350/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p350/r2.claim: A Persian couplet treats duha as the brightness of the Prophet's face and night as the darkness of his hair.
BURSEVI:v10p350/r2.anchor: والضحى رمزي زروي همو ماه مصطفى معنى والليل كيسوى سيه مصطفى

BURSEVI:v10p350/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p350/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p350/r3.claim: Night precedes in the preceding surah because darkness is the original state: day arises with the sun and the air returns to its first state when it sets; day leads here because of its intrinsic and incidental honor.
BURSEVI:v10p350/r3.anchor: وتقديم الليل في السورة المتقدمة باعتبار الأصل لأن النهار إنما يحدث بطلوع النير

BURSEVI:v10p350/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p350/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p350/r4.claim: Although duha is only one hour and night spans many, it equals the whole night as Muhammad equals all prophets; joy is brief while worldly sorrow and anxiety last longer.
BURSEVI:v10p350/r4.anchor: بأنه وإن كان ساعة من النهار لكنه يوازي جميع الليل كما إن محمدا عليه السلام يوازي جميع الأنبياء

BURSEVI:v10p350/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p350/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p350/r5.claim: A report says a black cloud over the Throne's left side rained grief for three hundred years, while a white cloud on the right rained joy for only an hour, explaining why sorrow is common and lasting and joy rare.
BURSEVI:v10p350/r5.anchor: أظلت غمامة سوداء عن يساره ونادت ماذا أمطر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā and the following Sūrah Alam Nashraḥ form a pair assuring the Prophet of success; the former reflects intense Makkan opposition, the latter emerging signs of success.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.claim: The discourse moves from day and night as models of developmental trials, to reassurance, promised better times, examples of past divine help, and duties arising from those favours.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.anchor: Following is the sequence of the discourse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p355/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p355/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p355/r1.claim: Al-Ḍuḥā is mid-morning, when people begin their daily work with renewed energy after a night’s rest.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p355/r1.anchor: refers to the time of mid-morning when people begin their daily routines and after resting the whole night start their day with a new vigour

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r1.claim: Day and night complement one another as divine mercy: night gives rest and day permits seeking bounty, sustaining the world together.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p356/r1.anchor: It is God’s great mercy that He created

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, and Ibn ʿĀmir open the endings in this sūrah, al-Layl, and al-Ḍuḥā.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر: بفتح أواخر آي هذه السورة

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r2.speaker: الكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī uses imālah throughout these endings and the endings of al-Layl and al-Ḍuḥā.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r2.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بإضجاع ذلك كله، وإضجاع أواخر سورة والليل

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r4.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ has several transmissions: some make the endings intermediate, while Warsh and Qālūn are also reported to open them all; another report opens only talāhā and inclines the rest.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع ذلك كله بين الفتح والكسر. وقال خلف عن إسحاق

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr is reported as using intermediate imālah, while ʿAbbās reports fully inclined forms for selected endings; other transmissions describe his treatment across verse endings.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r5.anchor: وقال اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو: ذلك كله بين الفتح والكسر

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r6.claim: Imālah is licensed where the alif behaves as one originating in yāʾ, as in derived verbs and nouns; an alif from wāw, such as العصا, normally resists it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r6.anchor: ولما كانت هذه في حكم الانقلاب عن الياء أجروا الألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r7.claim: Rare inclined examples with an alif from wāw are too uncommon to challenge the general pattern.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r7.anchor: فذلك من القلة بحيث لا يسوغ الاعتراض به

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p422/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p422/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p422/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr is reported with a fully inclined ending, while Nāfiʿ and another transmission from Abū ʿAmr are reported with intermediate or inclined forms; Abū ʿAlī refers back to the earlier discussion.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p422/r1.anchor: أبو عمرو: يكسرها في رواية عباس، نافع: بين الكسر والفتح

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r1.claim: The chapter has no reading difference here beyond imāla versus tafkhīm; al-Ḍuḥā is an oath.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr recites takbīr from the beginning of al-Ḍuḥā through the end of the Qurʾān, ending each sūra with Allāhu akbar and the basmala.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r2.anchor: وكان ابن كثير يكبر من اول هذه السورة إلى ان يختم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r3.claim: The cited account says revelation paused forty mornings; Quraysh claimed the Lord had abandoned Muhammad, then Gabriel's greeting and the Prophet's joy prompted the takbīr and the reassurance in al-Ḍuḥā.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p373#2/r3.anchor: ان الوحي أبطأ عنه اربعين صباحا فقال كفار قريش

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379/r1.claim: Qatada says the forenoon is one of the periods of the day.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p379/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ والضحى ﴾ قال ساعة من ساعات النهار

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r2.claim: Ḍuḥā may mean a daytime hour, the whole day, the forenoon prayer, or the time when Moses spoke to God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r2.anchor: ( والضحى ) : ساعة من النهار . أو النهار كل يسمى ضحى

SULAMI:v2p400/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400/r1.claim: Dawn is the unveiling of the inner secret by God, while the servant is occupied with calling people through attention to creation.
SULAMI:v2p400/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : مكاشفات سرك بنا ، واشتغالك بالدعوة نظرا إلى الخلق

SULAMI:v2p400/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p400/r2.claim: Dawn is the station of witnessing, and still night is the station of the inner eye associated with the Prophet's report that his heart is veiled.
SULAMI:v2p400/r2.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمه الله : والضحى هو مقام الأشهاد والليل إذا سجى مقام العين

TUSTARI:93:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:93:1/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:93:1/r1.claim: Inwardly, the morning brightness represents the spirit.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r3.claim: The surah is Meccan and follows the previous mention of the most pious, the Prophet, by recounting God's favors to him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p495/r3.anchor: هذه السورة مكية. ولما ذكر فيما قبلها وسيجنبها الأتقى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r1.claim: Al-ḍuḥā means the interval after sunrise when the sun has risen, rather than sunlight or the act of rising, because this fits what follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r1.anchor: والمراد به هنا وقت ارتفاع الشمس الذي يلي وقت بروزها للناظرين دون ضوئها وارتفاعها لأنه أنسب بما بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r2.claim: The time is a fitting oath because it is the day's youthful, vigorous phase and a daily honor for the sun.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r2.anchor: تخصيصه بالأقسام به لأنه شباب النهار وقوله فيه قوة غير قريبة من ضدها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r3.claim: Some say this was the hour God spoke to Moses and the sorcerers fell prostrate, linking the oath to God's continuing care and speech to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r3.anchor: ولأنه على ما قالوا الساعة التي كلم الله تعالى فيها موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r4.claim: An alternative takes ḍuḥā as the whole day, as in the verse about punishment arriving by day; the author objects that this passage contrasts it with a darkened night.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد به النهار كما في قوله تعالى أن يأتيهم بأسنا ضحى واعترض بالعرق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r5.claim: The objection to reading the whole day assumes without proof that the following night phrase requires intense darkness.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153#2/r5.anchor: وأجيبب بمنع دلالة القيد على الأشتداد وستسمع

BAGHAWI:93:1/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:93:1/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and has ten verses.

BAGHAWI:93:1/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r2.speaker: جندب بن سفيان
BAGHAWI:93:1/r2.claim: Jundub ibn Sufyan reports that after the Prophet was ill and did not rise for two or three nights, a woman taunted him that his Satan had left; then the opening verses were revealed.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r2.anchor: سمعت جندب بن سفيان قال : " اشتكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI:93:1/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:93:1/r3.claim: Another report identifies the woman who taunted the Prophet as Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن المرأة التي قالت ذلك أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب

BAGHAWI:93:1/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r4.speaker: المفسرون
BAGHAWI:93:1/r4.claim: The commentators say Jews asked the Prophet about Dhul-Qarnayn, the Companions of the Cave, and the Spirit; after he promised an answer the next day without saying God willing, revelation stopped.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r4.anchor: وقال المفسرون " سألت اليهود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI:93:1/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI:93:1/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Gabriel's delay was caused by a puppy in the Prophet's house; Gabriel explained that angels do not enter a house containing a dog or image.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r5.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم : كان سبب احتباس جبريل عليه السلام عنه

BAGHAWI:93:1/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r6.speaker: ابن جريج وابن عباس ومقاتل
BAGHAWI:93:1/r6.claim: Reports disagree about the duration of the revelation's delay: Ibn Jurayj says twelve days, Ibn Abbas fifteen, and Muqatil forty.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r6.anchor: فقال ابن جريج : اثنا عشر يوماً

BAGHAWI:93:1/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:93:1/r7.claim: When polytheists said God had abandoned and hated Muhammad, the surah was revealed; the Prophet said he missed Gabriel, who replied that he too yearned but was only a commanded servant.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r7.anchor: فقال المشركون : إن محمداً ودعه ربه وقلاه

BAGHAWI:93:1/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:93:1/r8.claim: The explanation concludes with God's statement that angels descend only by their Lord's command.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r8.anchor: فأنزل : { وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك

BAGHAWI:93:1/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:93:1/r9.claim: Al-duha can mean the whole day, since it is paired with the night; the verse about punishment arriving duha likewise means daytime.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r9.anchor: أقسم بالضحى وأراد به النهار كله

BAGHAWI:93:1/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:1/r10.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
BAGHAWI:93:1/r10.claim: Qatada and Muqatil instead interpret al-duha as the specific late-morning period, when the sun has risen and the day is temperate across seasons.
BAGHAWI:93:1/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل : يعني وقت الضحى

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r1.claim: The morning oath may mean the sun’s elevated hour, when daylight is strong, the time Moses spoke with God and the magicians prostrated, or daylight contrasted with nighttime.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:1-3/r1.anchor: { والضحى } ووقت ارتفاع الشمس وتخصيصه لأن النهار يقوى فيه

BINTSHATI:v1p23/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan without disagreement and is commonly placed eleventh in revelation order, after al-Fajr.
BINTSHATI:v1p23/r1.anchor: السورة مكية بلا خلاف، والمشهور أنها الحادية عشرة في ترتيب النزول. نزلت بعد الفجر

BINTSHATI:v1p24/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p24/r1.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
BINTSHATI:v1p24/r1.claim: The prevailing earlier view treats Qur'anic oaths as glorifying what is sworn by, since created things are great signs.
BINTSHATI:v1p24/r1.anchor: الرأي السائد عند الأقدمين، أن هذا القسم القرآني يحمل معنى التعظيم للمقسم به

BINTSHATI:v1p24/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p24/r3.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p24/r3.claim: Abduh explains the duha oath as drawing attention to the light's greatness and its status as a major sign and blessing.
BINTSHATI:v1p24/r3.anchor: فالقسم بالضياء للإشارة إلى تعظيم أمر الضياء وإعظام قدر النعمة فيه

BINTSHATI:v1p25/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p25/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p25/r3.claim: The oath's wāw can serve a rhetorical purpose beyond glorification: strongly directing attention to familiar sensory realities that prepare the reader for unseen meanings.
BINTSHATI:v1p25/r3.anchor: القسم بها يمكن أن يكون، والله أعلم، قد خرج عن أصل الوضع اللغوي في القسم للتعظيم، إلى معنى بياني

BINTSHATI:v1p25/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p25/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p25/r4.claim: The quality selected for the oath suits its context; any impression of glorification strengthens the attention rather than defining the device's main purpose.
BINTSHATI:v1p25/r4.anchor: واختيار المقسم به تراعى فيه الصفة التي تناسب الموقف

BINTSHATI:v1p26/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r1.claim: The daily alternation from bright duha to a quiet night is a sensory image that prepares for the unseen pause in revelation, without suggesting that heaven abandoned earth.
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r1.anchor: تألق الضوء في ضحوة النهار، ثم فتور الليل إذا سجا وسكن

BINTSHATI:v1p26/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r2.claim: The sensory contrast between light and darkness can clarify unseen guidance and truth or misguidance and falsehood.
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r2.anchor: معاني من الهدى والحق، أو الضلال والباطل، بماديات من النور والظلمة

BINTSHATI:v1p26/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r3.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي ونظام الدين النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r3.claim: They compare alternating night and day, which wax and wane by wisdom, to revelation being sent and withheld according to divine purposes.
BINTSHATI:v1p26/r3.anchor: فمرة تزداد ساعات الليل وتنقص ساعات النهار، ومرة بالعكس، فلا تكون الزيادة لهوى

BINTSHATI:v1p27/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r1.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي ونظام الدين النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r1.claim: They also say the oath answers the disbelievers' taunt: they were unable to prove their claim that God had abandoned Muhammad.
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r1.anchor: هاتوا الحجة، فعجزوا، فلزمه اليمين بأنه ما ودعه ربه ما قلاه

BINTSHATI:v1p27/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r2.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي ونظام الدين النيسابوري
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r2.claim: A further interpretation compares night and day alternately prevailing to how no created people are exempt from such change.
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r2.anchor: أنظر إلى جوار الليل مع النهار، لا يسلم أحدهما عن الآخر

BINTSHATI:v1p27/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r3.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r3.claim: Abduh says the Prophet's distress during the pause was relieved by renewed revelation: duha represents life-giving first revelation, while quiet night restores strength for later work.
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r3.anchor: فآتاه الله ما كان في شوق إليه، وثبته بالوحي وبشره أن تلك الفترة لم تكن عن ترك ولا عن قلى

BINTSHATI:v1p27/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r4.claim: The author's sensory analogy is nearly lost in Abduh's account of night as rest and preparation for work.
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r4.anchor: ويوشك الملحظ البيلني، أن يتوه وسط هذا الكلام في الضحى تقوى به الحياة

BINTSHATI:v1p27/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r5.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r5.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim comes close to matching the bright duha after darkness with revelation after its pause, but frames the oath as proof of God's lordship, wisdom, and mercy.
BINTSHATI:v1p27/r5.anchor: وكان "إبن قيم الجوزية" أقرب إلى إدراك الملحظ البياني

BINTSHATI:v1p28/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r1.claim: The author says Ibn al-Qayyim's appeal to doubts about God's lordship misses the stated occasion, which concerns a claim that God abandoned Muhammad.
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r1.anchor: الموقف كان ارتياباً من المشركين في ربوبية الله وحكمته ورحمته، وإنما كان - على قول المفسرين في سبب النزول - كلاماً

BINTSHATI:v1p28/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r2.claim: Some interpret the order of duha then night as preferring life until believers reach maturity, avoiding despair first and then fear of divine plotting.
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r2.anchor: إنه إشارة أن الحياة أولى للمؤمن من الموت إلى أن تحصل كمالاته الممكنة

BINTSHATI:v1p28/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r3.claim: The author finds no clear connection between the oath and its answer in the accounts of al-Tabari, al-Zamakhshari, and Abu Hayyan, and notes they do not compare it with God's explicit denials of oaths.
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r3.anchor: لم يتعرض "إبن جرير الطبري" لبيان ارتباط المقسم به

BINTSHATI:v1p28/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r4.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r4.claim: Al-Tabari reports disagreements over whether duha means the whole day or one daytime hour, and whether saja means night arriving, departing, settling, or becoming still.
BINTSHATI:v1p28/r4.anchor: فهم النهار كله، وهو ساعة من ساعات النهار

BINTSHATI:v1p29/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r1.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r1.claim: Al-Tabari selects daylight, understood as visible sunlight, for duha and stillness among its people for saja.
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r1.anchor: واختار "الطبري" من هذه الأقوال في الضحى

BINTSHATI:v1p29/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari defines duha as the early day when the sun rises and shines, while also reporting that it can mean the whole day; saja is settled darkness or quiet people and sounds.
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r2.anchor: هو صدر النهار حين ترتفع الشمس وتلقى شعاعها، وقيل: أريد بالضحى النهار

BINTSHATI:v1p29/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r6.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r6.claim: Abduh defines duha as sunlight in the day's prime and saja as the quiet and inactivity of night-time inhabitants.
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r6.anchor: هو ضوء الشمس في شباب النهار. وفي سجا الليل: هو ما تجده من سكون أهله

BINTSHATI:v1p29/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r7.claim: Although the words can carry several lexical senses, the rhetoric of this particular setting admits only the single sense that best fits it.
BINTSHATI:v1p29/r7.anchor: البلاغة لا تجيز إلا معنى واحداً في المقام الواحد

BINTSHATI:v1p30/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r1.claim: The sensory uses of the duha root center on visibility and exposure; most commonly, duha names the defined early daytime when the sun's light becomes clear, and it can name an act at that time.
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r1.anchor: ودلالة الوضوح هي الملحوظة في كل الإستعمالات الحسية للمادة

BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.claim: Qur'anic uses include duha opposite evening, the sun's light brought forth, and a specific time appointed for events; these usages weigh against interpreting it as the whole day.
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.anchor: وفي الاستعمال القرآني، نرى القرآن الكريم استعمل الضحى مقابلاً للعشية

BINTSHATI:v1p30/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r3.speaker: يعقوب
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r3.claim: Yaqub explains that the sacrificial day is called adha from the sheep sacrificed at duha.
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r3.anchor: وقال "يعقوب" في الأضحى: يسمى اليوم أضحى

BINTSHATI:v1p31/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p31/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p31/r1.claim: The appointment of people at duha in 20:59 and its use opposite evening in 79:46 show that duha means a specific daytime period, not the whole day; the same reading fits the sun's duha in 91:1.
BINTSHATI:v1p31/r1.anchor: مما يبعد تفسير الضحى بأنه النهار كله

BINTSHATI:v1p31/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p31/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p31/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says duha was chosen because it was when God spoke to Moses and when Moses met the sorcerers; the author rejects this anachronistic reading because the cited passages were revealed much later.
BINTSHATI:v1p31/r3.anchor: أقسم بالضحى، لأنها الساعة التي كلم فيها موسى عليه السلام

BINTSHATI:v1p32/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r1.speaker: النيسابوري والرازي
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r1.claim: Al-Nisaburi and al-Razi liken the duha hour to the whole night, just as Muhammad is said to equal all prophets and their communities.
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r1.anchor: توازي جميع الليل، كما أن محمداً - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يوازي جميع الأنبياء وأممهم

BINTSHATI:v1p32/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r2.claim: The author excludes esoteric readings that turn duha and night into the Prophet's face and hair, male and female relatives, knowledge and forgiveness, or Islam's rise and later estrangement.
BINTSHATI:v1p32/r2.anchor: ولا نقف بعد هذا عند تأويلات الإشاريين بأن الضحى وجه محمد، - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والليل شعره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451#s093/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451#s093/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451#s093/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to show that the most God-fearing person remains in divine favor in both lives through perfected qualities that lead to the goal.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451#s093/r1.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على آخر الليل بأن أتقى الأتقياء الذي هو الأتقى على الإطلاق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451#s093/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451#s093/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451#s093/r2.claim: The title al-Ḍuḥā captures this purpose because its physical daylight symbolizes the spiritual light of perfected character.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451#s093/r2.anchor: التي هي الإيصال للمقصود بما لها من النور المعنوي كالضحى بما له من النور الحسي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r1.claim: The oath by midmorning, the daylight’s finest and brightest portion, suits the most honored creature and signals his exceptional rank.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r1.anchor: فذكر ماهو أشرف النهار وألطفه وهو زهرته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r3.claim: The alternation of mixed and pure light and darkness can represent Qur’anic clear and ambiguous teachings and human spiritual conditions.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r3.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون الأول مشيرا إلى ما يأتي به هذا الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من المحكم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r4.claim: The heart’s light can overcome the soul’s darkness, while appetite can darken the whole person; spirit or temperament then elevates or degrades the person.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p452/r4.anchor: فروحه نور بنور القلب , فإن قويت شهوة النفس على نورانية القلب أظلم جميعه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p454/r2.claim: The opening’s hidden night recalls uncertainty about one’s path and destiny; remembering the signs and seeking refuge in God bring certainty.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r1.claim: The opening night evokes the beginning’s obscurity, while the manifest day evokes the clarity reached by people whose hearts God has strengthened.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r1.anchor: فلابتداء الأمر وشدة الإبهام والإظلام أشار قوله سبحانه وتعالى : { والليل إذا يغشى }

NAHHAS:v5p247/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p247/r1.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p247/r1.claim: He interprets al-ḍuḥā as the entire day.
NAHHAS:v5p247/r1.anchor: النهار كله قال أبو جعفر والمعروف عند العرب

NAHHAS:v5p247/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p247/r2.speaker: أبو روق
NAHHAS:v5p247/r2.claim: As transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, he glosses al-ḍuḥā as the morning's forenoon.
NAHHAS:v5p247/r2.anchor: المعروف عند العرب ما رواه أبو روق عن الضحاك قال الضحى ضحى النهار

NAHHAS:v5p247/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p247/r3.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v5p247/r3.claim: He says al-ḍuḥā is written only with final alif because it comes from ḍaḥā yaḍḥū.
NAHHAS:v5p247/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد والضحى يكتب بالألف لا غير لأنه من ضحا يضحو

NAHHAS:v5p247/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p247/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p247/r4.claim: He rejects the Kufan rule of writing yāʾ-root words with yāʾ: spelling should reflect pronunciation, and if it followed root origin then words from wāw roots would need wāw; Qurʾānic and conventional forms expose the inconsistency.
NAHHAS:v5p247/r4.anchor: وقول الكوفيين إنه بالياء لضم أوله وهذا قول لا يصح في معقول ولا قياس لأنه إن كتب على اللفظ فلفظه الألف وإن كتب على المعنى فهو راجع إلى الواو

NAHHAS:v5p247/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p247/r5.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v5p247/r5.claim: He argues that spelling records spoken form just as speech conveys what is in the mind, and cites rāmā and ghazā against root-based spelling.
NAHHAS:v5p247/r5.anchor: الكتابة إنما هي نقل ما في اللفظ كما أن اللفظ نقل ما في القلب

NAHHAS:v5p247/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p247/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v5p247/r6.claim: He summarizes the argument that writing yāʾ roots with yāʾ and wāw roots with alif follows neither pronunciation nor the muṣḥaf; the Qurʾānic spelling mā zakkā uses yāʾ.
NAHHAS:v5p247/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق وهذا معنى كلامه وما أعظم هذا الخطأ يعني قولهم يكتب ذوات الياء بالياء وذوات الواو بالألف فلا هم اتبعوا اللفظ كما يجب في الخط ولا هم اتبعوا المصحف فقد كتب في المصحف ما زكى بالياء

NAHHAS:v5p247/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p247/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v5p247/r7.claim: He adds that writing the dual rabā as rabayān contradicts the Qurʾānic form yarbū.
NAHHAS:v5p247/r7.anchor: يثنون ربا ربيان وهذا مخالف على كتاب الله

NAHHAS:v5p247/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p247/r8.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v5p247/r8.claim: He relays an allegation that al-Akhfash conspired with al-Kisāʾī to invent the spelling convention for profit and influence, after which it spread through al-Kisāʾī's political power.
NAHHAS:v5p247/r8.anchor: أن أبا الحسن الأخفش كان رجلا محتالا لشيء يأخذه فقال لأبي الحسن الكسائي قد استغنى من نحتاج إليه من النحو فنحتاج أن نجتمع على شيء نضطرهم إليه فاتفقا على هذا وأحدثاه ولم يكن قبلهما وشاع في الناس لتمكن الكسائي من السلطان

NAHHAS:v5p247/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p247/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p247/r9.claim: Imāla differs by reader: Ḥamza inclines yāʾ-root forms and darkens wāw-root forms, al-Kisāʾī inclines all, Abū ʿAmr follows the surah's pattern, and Medinans use a middle degree.
NAHHAS:v5p247/r9.anchor: حمزة يميل ما كان من ذوات الياء ويفخم ما كان من ذوات الواو والكسائي يميل الكل وأبو عمرو بن العلاء يتبع بعض الكلام بعضا فإن كانت السورة فيها ذوات الياء وذوات الواو أمال الكل والمدنيون يتوسطون

NAHHAS:v5p247/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p247/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p247/r10.claim: These approaches are all acceptable because verbs from wāw roots can be inclined when they shift to yāʾ in inflected forms, as ḍuḥā and sajā do.
NAHHAS:v5p247/r10.anchor: ليس في هذه المذاهب خطأ لأن ذوات الواو في الأفعال جائز إمالتها

DURR-FULL:v8p527/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r6.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r6.claim: The Prophet instructed them to pray the two midmorning rakʿahs using the Sun and Midmorning surahs.
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r6.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن عقبة بن عامر

DURR-FULL:v8p539/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and has eleven verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p539/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r2.claim: He said the surah was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال:

DURR-FULL:v8p539/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r3.claim: A transmission from the Prophet instructs reciters to pronounce takbir at the end of each surah, beginning when reaching al-Duha.
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r3.anchor: أخبره مجاهد أن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أمره بذلك

DURR-FULL:v8p539/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r4.speaker: جندب البجلي
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r4.claim: When the Prophet was ill and did not rise at night for two or three nights, a woman taunted him that his devil had abandoned him; the opening verses answered her.
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r4.anchor: والنسائي وابن جرير والطبراني والبيهقي وأبو نعيم معا في الدلائل عن جندب البجلي

DURR-FULL:v8p539/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r6.speaker: جندب
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r6.claim: When Gabriel was withheld, a cousin's daughter said the Prophet's companion had left him; the passage was revealed.

DURR-FULL:v8p539/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r7.speaker: جندب
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r7.claim: After a stone injured his finger and the Prophet stopped night prayer for two or three nights, a woman blamed his devil's departure; al-Tirmidhi authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v8p539/r7.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي وصححه وابن أبي حاتم واللفظ له عن جندب

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r1.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r1.claim: After Abu Lahab's surah, his wife confronted the Prophet; when revelation paused and she said his companion had abandoned and hated him, the opening verses were revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r1.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم عن زيد بن أرقم

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r2.claim: He reports Khadija saying that the Prophet's Lord seemed to have rejected him, after which the verses were revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن عبد الله بن شداد

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r3.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r3.claim: When Gabriel was delayed and the Prophet became distressed, Khadija inferred from his distress that God had rejected him; the surah followed.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر عن عروة

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r5.claim: After revelation paused for days, polytheists taunted that God had abandoned Muhammad; the passage came down, and the night ‘when it settles’ means when it arrives.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن مردويه من طريق العوفي عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r6.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r6.claim: Their mursal reports give the same occasion: a pause in revelation prompted the claim that God had abandoned Muhammad, answered by this passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير نحوه من مرسل قتادة والضحاك

DURR-FULL:v8p540/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r7.claim: He glossed the midmorning light as an hour of daylight and the night as quiet among people.
DURR-FULL:v8p540/r7.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.speaker: أم حفص
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.claim: A dead puppy hidden beneath the Prophet's bed delayed revelation for four days; after Khawla found it, the Prophet trembled and the passage through ‘you will be satisfied’ came down.
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة في مسنده والطبراني وابن مردويه عن أم حفص عن أمها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r1.claim: Jundub reports that after the Prophet missed night prayer for one or two nights, a woman taunted him that his devil had left; the sura was revealed to reassure him that God had neither abandoned nor hated him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r1.anchor: عن الاسود بن قيس قال : سمعت جندبا يقول : اشتكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r2.claim: A second Jundub report says a stone injured the Prophet's finger; after two or three nights without rising, a woman said his devil had left, and the same verses were revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3442/r2.anchor: حدثني الاسود بن قيس ، انه سمع جندبا يقول : رمى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحجر في اصبعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r1.claim: The oath rebuts the idolaters' claim that revelation stopped when the Prophet did not recite the Quran at night for several days; the warning targets their insinuation, since the Prophet himself had no doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r1.anchor: القسم لتأكيد الخبر ردا على زعم المشركين أن الوحي انقطع عن النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r2.claim: Morning brightness evokes revelation and guidance, while night evokes the Prophet's Quran recitation that nearby idolaters heard; the time when night settled may be when he prayed, as in al-Muzzammil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r2.anchor: ومناسبة القسم ب { الضحى والليل } أن الضحى وقت انبثاق نور الشمس فهو إيماء إلى تمثيل نزول الوحي وحصول الاهتداء به ، وأن الليل وقت قيام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r3.claim: The term ضحى was explained at al-Shams 1.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r3.anchor: والضحى تقدم بيانه عند قوله تعالى : { والشمس وضحاها } ( الشمس : 1 ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r4.claim: The muṣḥaf writes the final alif of الضحى in the yāʾ shape although its root vowel is wāw, matching other word endings, most of which derive from yāʾ, and supporting imāla in relevant dialects; Ibn Mālik discusses the orthographic pattern.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p394#2/r4.anchor: وكتب في المصحف { والضحى } بألف في صورة الياء مع أن أصل ألفه الواو لأنهم راعوا المناسبة مع أكثر الكلمات المختومة بألف في هذه السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r6.claim: Its message serves as evidence for al-Duha: past care reassures the Prophet that the One who began blessing him will continue it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p407/r6.anchor: فمضمونها شبيه بأنه حجة على مضمون سورة الضحى تثبيتا له بتذكيره سالف عنايته به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r1.claim: Duha was explained earlier as the rise and strength of light.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r1.anchor: تقدم تفسير الضحى بأنه سطوع الضوء وعظمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r2.claim: Qatada takes duha here as the whole daytime.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: الضحى هنا، النهار كله،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p156/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p156/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p156/r2.claim: Alternatively, it means the beginning of the day.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p156/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p156/r3.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p156/r3.claim: Alternatively, it means the first hour of the day, when the sun has moved on.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p156/r3.anchor: أول ساعة من النهار إذا ترحلت الشمس قاله السدي ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p156/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p156/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p156/r4.claim: Alternatively, it means the whole day.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r1.claim: After the Prophet did not rise for one or two nights while ill, a woman accused his devil of abandoning him; the Prophet's report says the opening verses were then revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r1.anchor: فقالت: يا محمد، ما أرى شيطانك إلا قد تركك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r2.speaker: مشركون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r2.claim: In another version, Gabriel's delay led the polytheists to say Muhammad had been abandoned, and the verses were revealed in response.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r2.anchor: قال: أبطأ جبريل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال المشركون: ودع محمد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r3.claim: Another narration says a stone injured the Prophet's finger, after which he stopped night worship for two or three nights and a woman made the same accusation; Ibn Kathir calls the injury report authentic but the causal link unusual.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r3.anchor: رمي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحجر في أصبعه فقال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the woman who made the accusation was Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p424/r4.anchor: قيل: إن هذه المرأة هي: أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r2.claim: God swears by the forenoon and its light, and by night when it settles, darkens, and grows still.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r2.anchor: وهذا قسم منه تعالى بالضحى وما جعل فيه من الضياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r4.claim: The contrasting light of day and darkness of night visibly demonstrate the Creator's power.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p425/r4.anchor: وذلك دليل ظاهر على قدرة خالق هذا وهذا

JISHUMI:v10p7449/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r1.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet promises intercession and reward for reciting Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā, scaled to the number of every orphan and asker.
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r1.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (الضحى) جعله الله فيمن يشفع له محمد

JISHUMI:v10p7449/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r2.claim: The previous chapter ends with God pleasing the most pious through reward; this one addresses the Prophet and promises him rank and honor at the Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r2.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (والليل) بأنه يرضي الأتقى بما يعطيه من الثواب، افتتح هذه السورة خطابا للنبي

JISHUMI:v10p7449/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r8.claim: Ḍuḥā is the start of the day and derives from appearing in sunlight.
JISHUMI:v10p7449/r8.anchor: الضحى: صدر النهار، وأصله الظهور، يقال: ضحى فلان للشمس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r1.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says duha is the first hour of day, when the sun has moved onward.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنه أول ساعة من النهار إذا ترحلت الشمس , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r2.claim: Qatada says duha is the beginning of the day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه صدر النهار , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r3.speaker: قطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r3.anchor: الثالث : هو طلوع الشمس , قاله قطرب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says duha is the daylight over the whole day; Ali ibn Isa connects this to the expression for someone appearing in the sun.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p291#2/r4.anchor: الرابع : هو ضوء النهار في اليوم كله , مأخوذ من قولهم ضحى فلان الشمس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#6/r1.claim: Duha is the early part of the day, when the sun has risen higher; it may be singled out because Moses spoke and the magicians fell prostrate at that hour.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#6/r1.anchor: المراد به وقت الضحى وهو صدر النهار حين ترتفع الشمس وإنما خص وقت الضحى بالقسم لأنها الساعة التى كلم فيها موسى عليه السلام وألقى فيها السحرة سجدا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#6/r2.claim: Alternatively, duha denotes the whole day, paired with night in the following oath.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#6/r2.anchor: أو النهار كله لمقابلته بالليل فى قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r1.claim: Duha means daytime here, as the verse pairs it with night; the Qur'an likewise contrasts a night attack with a daytime one.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r1.anchor: والمراد به النهار لقوله { والليل إذا سجى } فقابله بالليل.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r2.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل وجعفر الصادق
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r2.claim: Qatada, Muqatil, and Ja'far al-Sadiq say the oath invokes the morning when God spoke to Moses and the night of the Ascension.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل وجعفر الصادق: أقسم بالضحى الذي كلم الله فيه موسى، وبليلة المعراج.

QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r3.claim: Another view identifies duha as the hour when the magicians fell prostrate, supported by the command to assemble people at duha.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r3.anchor: وقيل: هي الساعة التي خر فيها السحرة سجدا. بيانه قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r4.claim: Semantic scholars understand an omitted oath object: the sense is by the Lord of the morning and its like.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:1-3/r4.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني فيه وفي أمثاله: فهي إضمار، مجازه ورب الضحى.

QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r1.claim: The Meccan surah is wholly a tender consolation for the Prophet, renewing hope, closeness, reassurance, and calm for his weary spirit.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r1.anchor: إنها كلها خالصة للنبي [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] كلها نجاء له من ربه

QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r2.speaker: روايات كثيرة
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r2.claim: Many reports say revelation paused and Gabriel was delayed; the polytheists then claimed that Muhammad’s Lord had abandoned him, and the surah was revealed in response.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r2.anchor: ورد في روايات كثيرة أن الوحي فتر عن رسول الله

QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r3.claim: Revelation and Gabriel’s visits were the Prophet’s provision and spiritual refreshment through the hardships of rejection, hostility, and persecution; their pause left him isolated and distressed.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r3.anchor: والوحي ولقاء جبريل والاتصال بالله ، كانت هي زاد الرسول

QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r4.claim: The message assures him that God never deserted or hated him, that the afterlife is better, and that his Lord will give until he is content, recalling prior care as proof.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r4.anchor: وما تركك ربك من قبل أبدا ، وما قلاك من قبل قط ، وما أخلاك من رحمته

QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r5.claim: Dawn and the settled night form a delicate frame for tenderness and reflection; their clear, pure moments let the spirit sense creation worshipping its Maker, matching the surah’s emotional setting.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r5.anchor: جعل الإطار من الضحى الرائق ، ومن الليل الساجي . أصفى آنين من آونة الليل والنهار

QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r6.claim: The oath links cosmic phenomena with human feeling and makes the Prophet feel accompanied rather than forsaken or alone in the living universe.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r6.anchor: فيعيش ذلك القلب في أنس من هذا الوجود ، غير موحش ولا غريب فيه فريد

QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r7.claim: The surah’s graceful wording and musical cadence embody its gentleness; the beauty of this artistic expression points to God’s unmatched creative work.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:1/r7.anchor: إن هذا الإبداع في كمال الجمال ليدل على الصنعة . صنعة الله التي لا تماثلها صنعة

RAZI-FULL:v31p188/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p188/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p188/r1.claim: Exegetes take الضحى either as the midmorning, when the sun rises and spreads its light, or as the whole daytime, contrasted with the whole night.
RAZI-FULL:v31p188/r1.anchor: المراد بالضحى وقت الضحى وهو صدر النهار

RAZI-FULL:v31p189/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p189/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p189/r4.claim: Midmorning is when people gather and find ease after the isolation of night, so it promises revelation and comfort after the Prophet's anxiety during its pause.
RAZI-FULL:v31p189/r4.anchor: أنه وقت اجتماع الناس وكمال الأنس بعد الاستيحاش في زمان الليل

RAZI-FULL:v31p189/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p189/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p189/r5.claim: Midmorning recalls the hour Moses spoke with God and the sorcerers prostrated; the God who honored Moses can honor Muhammad and turn his enemies' hearts.
RAZI-FULL:v31p189/r5.anchor: أنها الساعة التي كلم فيها موسى ربه

STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r1.claim: Al-Ḍuḥā is early Makkan and ranked fourth by many, seventh by others; it may be the first sūrah revealed whole, though others give that distinction to al-Fātiḥah.
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r1.anchor: considered by many commentators to be fourth (others say seventh) in the chronological order of revelation and perhaps the first sūrah to be revealed in full at one time

STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r2.speaker: most
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r2.claim: The title most commonly means the rising sun's light; it can also mean the period from daybreak to noon, the whole sunlit day, or all creation made visible by sunlight. It also names a late-morning supererogatory prayer.
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r2.anchor: most common understanding of al-ḍuḥā as a reference to the light of the rising sun, but it can also refer to the period from daybreak until noon

STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r3.speaker: several commentators
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r3.claim: One occasion account says revelation paused for twelve, forty, or fifty days, after which an idolater taunted Muhammad that his satan had forsaken him, prompting reassurance.
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r3.anchor: According to several commentators, the Prophet had not received a revelation for some time (some say twelve days, others forty, and others fifty)

STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r4.claim: Another account says idolaters declared that Muhammad's Lord had forsaken and despised him.
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r4.anchor: Others say that it was in response to several idolaters saying, “Surely Muhammad’s lord has forsaken him and despised him”

STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r5.claim: A further account says illness kept the Prophet from night vigil for two or three nights; Umm Jamīl, Abū Lahab's wife, taunted him, and vv. 1–3 were revealed.
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r5.anchor: the Prophet became sick and could not offer his supererogatory night vigil

STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah consoles the Prophet: it assures him God will not abandon him, recalls God's favors, and ends by urging care for the downtrodden and preaching the message.
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.anchor: The main theme of the sūrah is consolation of the Prophet. It begins with an assertion that God would not abandon the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:93:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:1/r1.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:93:1/r1.claim: Some identify morning brightness with the morning God spoke to Moses and night with the Night Journey and Ascension; others identify it as the moment Moses' opponents recognized truth and prostrated.
STUDYQURAN:93:1/r1.anchor: others say al-ḍuḥā refers to the hour at which

STUDYQURAN:93:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:1/r2.speaker: al-Shawkānī
STUDYQURAN:93:1/r2.claim: When al-ḍuḥā precedes the night, al-Shawkānī says it refers to the whole day.
STUDYQURAN:93:1/r2.anchor: According to al-Shawkānī, when al-ḍuḥā precedes the mention of night, as in this context, it refers to the entire day.

STUDYQURAN:93:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:1/r3.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:93:1/r3.claim: Other symbolic readings make morning the Garden's light and night the Fire's darkness, or light in knowers' hearts and blackness in disbelievers' hearts.
STUDYQURAN:93:1/r3.anchor: It is also said that al-ḍuḥā is the light of the Garden and the night is the darkness of the Fire

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.claim: Some say Sūrahs 93 and 94 were originally one, since Companions recited them together in one prayer cycle without a basmalah separating them.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r3.anchor: the Companions of the Prophet would recite them together in a single prayer cycle

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.claim: Both sūrahs present God's bounties as relief: Sūrah 93 addresses external needs, Sūrah 94 spiritual relief; 94 recalls blessings, reassures, then commands exertion and turning to God.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.anchor: Thematically both sūrahs speak of the bounties that God has provided the Prophet Muhammad as relief for the difficulties that beset him

TAB-FULL:v24p481#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p481#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p481#2/r1.claim: The oath is by the ḍuḥā, which he takes to mean the whole daytime, based on the expression for being exposed to the sun; another view restricts it to the forenoon hour.
TAB-FULL:v24p481#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {والضحى} [الضحى: 1] : ساعة من ساعات النهار

TAB-FULL:v24p481#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p481#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p481#2/r2.claim: Qatadah takes the ḍuḥā as one of the daytime hours.
TAB-FULL:v24p481#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {والضحى} [الضحى: 1] : ساعة من ساعات النهار

TAB-FULL:v24p484#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p484#2/r3.speaker: جندب بن عبد الله البجلي
TAB-FULL:v24p484#2/r3.claim: When revelation was delayed, a woman said Muhammad had been abandoned or left by Satan; God sent down the opening of the sūrah to refute the claim.
TAB-FULL:v24p484#2/r3.anchor: أبطأ جبريل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالت امرأة

THALABI:v10p223/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p223/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p223/r1.claim: A woman taunted Muhammad that his Satan had abandoned him after he had not prayed at night for two or three nights; one report identifies her as Umm Jamil, and the sura was revealed in response.
THALABI:v10p223/r1.anchor: فمكث ليلتين أو ثلاثا لا يقوم [الليل] ، فقالت له امرأة: يا محمد ما أرى شيطانك إلا قد تركك

THALABI:v10p223/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p223/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p223/r2.claim: Duha can mean the whole daytime, inferred from its contrast with night; another view makes it the midmorning when the sun is high and the day moderate in temperature.
THALABI:v10p223/r2.anchor: فأنزل الله سبحانه والضحى. يعني النهار كله

THALABI:v10p223/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p223/r3.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
THALABI:v10p223/r3.claim: They define duha as the hour when the sun has risen and the day's heat or cold is moderate.
THALABI:v10p223/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل: يعني وقت الضحى، وهي الساعة التي فيها ارتفاع الشمس، واعتدال النهار من الحر والبرد

THALABI:v10p223/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p223/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p223/r4.claim: Other views identify it as the hour God spoke to Moses or the hour the magicians fell prostrate, when people were assembled.
THALABI:v10p223/r4.anchor: وقيل: هي الساعة التي كلم الله فيها موسى، وقيل: هي الساعة التي ألقي السحرة فيها سجدا

THALABI:v10p223/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p223/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v10p223/r5.claim: They understand both oaths with an implied 'Lord': by the Lord of morning and night.
THALABI:v10p223/r5.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني فيه وفي أمثاله: بإضمار الرب مجازه: ورب الضحى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p97#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p97#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p97#2/r1.claim: The meaning of duha was explained in the discussion of the sun and its duha.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p97#2/r1.anchor: قد تقدم تفسيره عند قوله: {والشمس وضحاها}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p409/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p409/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p409/r3.claim: Duḥā is the time when the sun rises high after sunrise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p409/r3.anchor: الضحى في اللغة: هو وقت ارتفاع الشمس بعد الشروق

ELMALILI:93:1/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:1/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:1/r1.claim: Duha is the familiar midmorning, when the sun begins to shine and rise and the day is in its youthful phase.
ELMALILI:93:1/r1.anchor: “Duhâ” diye mâruf olan kuşluk zamanına ki Güneş’in parlayıp yükselmeye başladığı, gündüzün gençliği zamanıdır.

ELMALILI:93:1/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:1/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:1/r2.claim: The definite article may be generic, but in this address to the Prophet it more likely points to the singular dawn of truth: the Muhammadan mission beginning to radiate mercy and light to the worlds.
ELMALILI:93:1/r2.anchor: Hitab Resûlullah’a olmak itibariyle bu ahd mânası râcih olur.

ELMALILI:93:1/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:1/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:1/r3.claim: Others connect the oath to the Prophet's face or divine speech; the verse about people gathering at duha also evokes the appointed morning when Moses overcame the magicians.
ELMALILI:93:1/r3.anchor: vech-i Muhammedîye veya teklîm-i ilâhî zamanına işaret olduğu da söylenmiştir. Nitekim طٰهٰ’da وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًۭى

ELMALILI:93:2-4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:2-4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:2-4/r12.claim: Duha expresses the bright, youthful joy of life and revealed knowledge, while the settled night signals rest before a promised renewal; this relation fittingly introduces the assurance that the Lord has not abandoned Muhammad.
ELMALILI:93:2-4/r12.anchor: gecenin dindiği sükûnu hengâmına kasem olsun ki yâ Muhammed

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:1/r1.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:1/r1.claim: Most commentators take duha as the whole daytime, the counterpart of night in verse 2.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:1/r1.anchor: Duhâ kelimesi “kuşluk” anlamına gelmekle birlikte çoğu müfessirler, 2. âyetteki “gece”nin alternatifi olarak burada bütünüyle gündüz vakti için kullanıldığı kanaatindedirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:1/r2.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:1/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur takes duha as morning here too, alluding to revelation's light spreading through the world like the morning sun covering the earth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:1/r2.anchor: İbn Âşûr’a göre ise kelime burada da kuşluk vaktini ifade etmekte olup, bununla, tıpkı kuşluk vakti güneş ışığının yeryüzünü bütünüyle kaplaması gibi vahiy ışığının da dünyaya inip aydınlatmaya başladığına imada bulunulmuştur

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r1.speaker: جندب
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r1.claim: Jundub reports that when the Prophet was ill and did not rise for one or two nights, a woman said his Satan had abandoned him, and the opening verses of al-Duha were revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r1.anchor: اشتكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلة أو ليلتين فأتته امرأة فقالت يا محمد ما أرى شيطانك إلا قد تركك

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r2.speaker: جندب
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r2.claim: In another report, Gabriel was delayed and the polytheists said Muhammad had been abandoned, prompting the revelation.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r2.anchor: أبطأ جبريل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال المشركون قد ودع محمد فنزلت

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam reports that after Gabriel did not descend for days, Umm Jamil, Abu Lahab's wife, said the Prophet had been abandoned and rejected, and the verses were revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r3.anchor: مكث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أياما لا ينزل عليه جبريل فقالت أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r4.speaker: خولة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r4.claim: Khawla's report says a dead puppy under the bed delayed revelation for four days; after it was removed Gabriel came, and verses through “until you are satisfied” were revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r4.anchor: أن جروا دخل بيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فدخل تحت السرير فمات فمكث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعة أيام لا ينزل عليه الوحي

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r5.speaker: ابن حجر
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r5.claim: Ibn Hajar says the puppy story as a cause of revelation is unusual and anomalous, rejected because it conflicts with sound reports, although the delay due to a puppy is well known.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r5.anchor: ولكن كونها سبب نزول الآية غريب بل شاذ مردود بما في الصحيح

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r6.claim: Abdullah ibn Shaddad reports that Khadija told the Prophet she thought his Lord had rejected him, and then the surah was revealed; this report is mursal.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r6.anchor: أن خديجة قالت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أرى ربك إلا قد قلاك فنزلت

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r7.speaker: عروة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r7.claim: Urwa's mursal report says delayed revelation distressed the Prophet and Khadija compassionately told him she thought his Lord had rejected him; Ibn Hajar says Umm Jamil said it spitefully while Khadija said it out of concern.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230#2/r7.anchor: لكن أم جميل قالته شماتة وخديجة قالته توجعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r2.claim: The following sūra was revealed after revelation had stopped for a period; three explanations are offered for the pause: the Prophet had promised answers about Dhū al-Qarnayn, the Cave Companions, and the Spirit without saying “God willing”; a companion's lack of cleanliness; or a puppy in his house.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r2.anchor: اتفق المفسرون على أن هذه [ السورة ] نزلت بعد انقطاع الوحي مدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam specifically attributes the pause in revelation to a puppy in the Prophet's house.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r3.anchor: والثالث لأجل جرو كان في بيته قاله زيد بن أسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r4.speaker: جندب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r4.claim: In a report in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, a Qurashī woman taunted that the Prophet's devil had abandoned him, after which the opening verses of al-Ḍuḥā were revealed; she was Umm Jamīl, Abū Lahab's wife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p153/r4.anchor: وروى البخاري ومسلم في الصحيحين من حديث جندب قال قالت امرأة من قريش للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r1.claim: Duha is the early part of the day, until the sun rises high and spreads its light.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r1.anchor: المراد بالضحى : وقت الضحى ، وهو صدر النهار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r2.claim: The forenoon may be singled out because Moses was addressed and the magicians prostrated at that hour, as in 20:59.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r2.anchor: وقيل : إنما خص وقت الضحى بالقسم ، لأنها الساعة التي كلم فيها موسى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r3.claim: Duha may mean daytime generally, as in the contrast with night in 7:98.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p770/r3.anchor: وقيل : أريد بالضحى : النهار ، بيانه قوله : { أن يأتيهم بأسنا ضحى }

TABRISI:93:5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، عروة بن الزبير
TABRISI:93:5/r1.claim: A noncanonical reading attributed to the Prophet and ʿUrwa lightens the consonant in mā waddaʿaka; the standard reading doubles it.
TABRISI:93:5/r1.anchor: في الشواذ عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعروة بن الزبير ما ودعك بالتخفيف

TABRISI:93:5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5/r5.speaker: ابن جني، سيبويه
TABRISI:93:5/r5.claim: Ibn Jinnī says the light verb wadaʿ is rare; Sībawayh says Arabic uses taraka instead and cites a line of Abū al-Aswad.
TABRISI:93:5/r5.anchor: وقال سيبويه: استغنوا عن وزر وودع بقولهم ترك

TABRISI:93:5/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5/r9.claim: Sajā means becoming still and calm; poetry describes a tranquil sea and a quiet night.
TABRISI:93:5/r9.anchor: السجو السكون يقال: سجى يسجو إذا هدأ وسكن

TABRISI:93:5#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5#2/r1.claim: The oath's ḍuḥā means the whole daylight, shown by its contrast with night as it settles.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r1.anchor: أقسم سبحانه بنور النهار كله من قولهم ضحى فلان للشمس إذ ظهر لها

TABRISI:93:5#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5#2/r2.claim: Other views take ḍuḥā as the first hour of morning, the opening part of the day, or the Lord of morning and settled night.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r2.anchor: المراد بالضحى أول ساعة من النهار

THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.claim: They report that Jews asked about Dhū al-Qarnayn, the Cave Companions, and the Spirit; the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying “if God wills,” and revelation paused.
THALABI:v10p222#3/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: سألت اليهود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف وعن الروح

THALABI:v10p222#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p222#3/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v10p222#3/r2.claim: He says Gabriel’s delay was because a puppy was in the Prophet’s house; Gabriel explained that angels do not enter a house with a dog or image.
THALABI:v10p222#3/r2.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: كان سبب احتباس جبرائيل (عليه السلام) كون جرو في بيته

THALABI:v10p222#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p222#3/r3.speaker: ابن حريج
THALABI:v10p222#3/r3.claim: He gives the duration of the revelation pause as twelve days.

THALABI:v10p222#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p222#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p222#3/r4.claim: He gives the duration of the revelation pause as fifteen days.
THALABI:v10p222#3/r4.anchor:
وقال ابن عباس:
خمسة عشر يوما

THALABI:v10p222#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p222#3/r5.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v10p222#3/r5.claim: He gives the duration of the revelation pause as forty days.
THALABI:v10p222#3/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أربعين يوما. قالوا: فقال المشركون:

THALABI:v10p222#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p222#3/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p222#3/r6.claim: Another reported duration is twenty-five days; polytheists then taunted that the Prophet’s Lord had abandoned and hated him.
THALABI:v10p222#3/r6.anchor:
يوما. قالوا: فقال
المشركون: إن محمدا ودعه ربه وقلاه

THALABI:v10p222#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p222#3/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p222#3/r7.claim: When Muslims asked why revelation had stopped, he replied that revelation could not descend while they neglected cleaning between their fingers and trimming their nails.
THALABI:v10p222#3/r7.anchor: ينزل علي الوحي وأنتم لا تنقون براجمكم ولا تقلمون أظفاركم

THALABI:v10p222#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p222#3/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p222#3/r8.claim: When Gabriel arrived with this surah, the Prophet said he had missed him; Gabriel replied that he too had longed for him but only descended by God’s command.
THALABI:v10p222#3/r8.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يا جبرائيل ما جئت حتى اشتقت إليك» ، فقال جبرائيل (عليه السلام) : وأنا كنت

THALABI:v10p243/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p243/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p243/r3.claim: The sequence after “Read” and al-Muddaththir was al-Qalam through “you are of great character,” then al-Ḍuḥā.
THALABI:v10p243/r3.anchor: ثم كان ما نزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن بعد اقرأ والمدثر، ن والقلم إلى قوله: وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم، ثم

THALABI:v10p243/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p243/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
THALABI:v10p243/r4.claim: He says revelation began with al-ʿAlaq, then Gabriel paused; after Khadīja feared the Prophet had been abandoned, al-Ḍuḥā was revealed.
THALABI:v10p243/r4.anchor: عبد الله بن شداد قال: نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرأ باسم ربك، ثم أبطأ عليه جبرائيل، فقالت له

ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r4.claim: The Morning is Meccan and unanimously counted as eleven verses; it follows the mention of the most God-fearing with God's gifts to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r4.anchor: مكية وآيها إحدى عشرة آية بلا خلاف ولما ذكر سبحانه فيما قبلها وسيجنبها الأتقى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r5.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r5.claim: The Imam says the preceding surah concerns Abū Bakr and this one the Messenger, with no intervening surah to show no intermediary between them; precedence of Abū Bakr's surah does not imply superiority, just as an oath by creation may precede an oath by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r5.anchor: وقال الإمام لما كانت الأولى سورة أبي بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه وهذه سورة رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عقب جل وعلا بها ولم يجعل بينهما واسطة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r6.claim: Alusi dismisses the Imam's flower metaphor as a claim that cannot withstand scrutiny.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p153/r6.anchor: ثم أن ما ذكره زهرة ربيع لا تتحمل الفرك كما لا يخفى
